title: Can’t Read the Room
text: “Now then, it seems Wolf has ended up becoming the Claw Hero, but more importantly, we need to deal with Takt.”
“What are you planning to do?”
“Ah, don’t be foolish… this isn’t something you want to get involved in.”
“But can we really just leave him be?”

“Or rather, wouldn’t it be kinder to just kill this man quickly? That’s starting to feel like the right call… Wolf seems to have some sort of moving, story-worthy backstory, and I’d really love to dig into all the details up close as another page in the legend of Shield Hero.”
Rabbit Guy kept glancing over at the Takt bunch, now skewered together like a three-colored dango on my spear, but I paid it no mind.
“Honestly, it just doesn’t feel right unless Wolf is the one to finish him off. You, sir, truly cannot read the room at all.”
“What’s that? You have a complaint, do you?”
Rabbit Guy immediately darted behind Crocodile Guy and Father for cover.
“Ah… Motoyasu-kun. I get that this guy needs to suffer, but what exactly are you planning to do?”
“Right. If I finish him off here, Takt’s remnants will scatter and run wild across the world, so I need to handle the aftermath properly, indeed.”
Otherwise it’d be a real headache. Takt had to be made to suffer as much as possible. And for that, I needed to deal with his remnants before they could cause trouble.
“The Claw Hero is from Siltvelt, right? So does that mean Wolf’s going to have to go report Takt’s misdeeds over there from now on?”
“That’s how it’ll go… but we need proof that will convince people, on the surface, that the Whip Hero committed crimes and was hiding multiple Seven Star Weapons.”

I’d later learn that Wolf—Magalum—was, compared to his rather scatterbrained brother, a bit more studious and quick-witted, and apparently far better at negotiation. Something about having handled the social side of things for a brother who was hopeless with people.

“That part will all be settled once we head to Faubrey, I say. We just take this one captive as is, bring him before the Pig King of Faubrey, and strip him of his titles right in front of everyone. And wouldn’t you know it, even now he’s still carrying both the Whip and the Hammer.”

If two weapons came off of Takt at the moment of his stripping in the name of the Legendary Weapons, that would be irrefutable proof. After that, we could just leave it to the Pig King and ship off the whole lot of Takt’s pigs at once.
“Guh!! Guhh!!!”

The Takt bunch struggled desperately, but I wasn’t about to let them off. From here on, you’re all headed straight for the pig processing plant. Wolf was looking at me like he couldn’t believe what he was seeing, but that was surely just my imagination. This was the killer of the brother he respected, after all. Since he was presumably also a card-carrying member of the Takt Victims Association, I figured I’d let him watch this one suffer to his heart’s content.
“I guess it’s fine since he’s already got a way to socially annihilate the guy figured out…”
“I sympathize deeply, but just from listening, this fellow sounds like a thoroughly wicked man.”
“It does seem that way. If his crimes are exposed and proper punishment is dealt out, there doesn’t seem to be much need for us to go waving the banner of justice ourselves.”
“Kuun.”
Even with his memories restored, Wolf just kept hiding behind Father, whimpering something under his breath.
“How much longer is this filth going to stay stuck to my spear, I say!”

I gave it a swing and yanked the three-colored dango loose. Right, then—as a little harassment toward the spirit of the spear, let’s just jam it right into Takt’s backside. I drove it home with a satisfying thunk, expanding his rear quite generously.
“—Gyaaah!!!”
“What an unreasonable thing to do… no one’s going to be able to stop him at this point. Motoyasu-kun… um, maybe take it easy?”
“Even an order from Father himself cannot be obeyed on this point. No mercy may be shown to Takt.”

No matter what mercy one showed Takt, the word ‘gratitude’ simply wasn’t in his vocabulary. From what I understood, reincarnators like him apparently received some kind of power from the Crimson Swine’s main body, but judging from his personality up to this point, he almost certainly never felt a shred of gratitude for it. In any case, I pulled out some rope and bound up the Takt bunch tight. Of course, I kept up the silence effect with Silence Lance as well. If the paralysis wore off even a little, he might try to escape with some skill or another, after all.
“There’s plenty left to deal with, but let’s get ready to depart, I say.”
The dragon, the griffin, the fox, and the pig corpses all needed disposing of.
“This turned into quite the dangerous conversation, starting from celebrating Shion joining the arena…”
“Ah… how exactly did we get from there to Wolf’s origins and the whole Claw Hero business…”
“I suppose it’s all connected somehow, but it really does feel like several steps got skipped over amid all that overwhelming violence.”
“Kuun… I was supposed to be the one to take him down…”

I called on Yuki-chan and the others to help prepare the carriage, since we needed to head to Faubrey without delay. It would’ve been nice to just take the Portal there, but enslaving Takt wasn’t currently an option.
“You were taking so long I came to check on you… ah, I see. So you got tangled up with this one.”
At that moment, of all people, Rafumi showed up together with Filo-tan. Right, I remembered now—she’d come by to visit our base.
“Hm? What’re you guys doing?”
“Er… Filo, you don’t need to worry about this. Go chat with Shion and the others over there for a bit, Theo too.”
“Ehh…”
Filo-tan was still wary of Rabbit Guy.
“I see. Well then, what shall we talk about?”
“Talking with the usapil guy and Shion-oniichan? Are the usapil guy’s ears tasty?”
“They are not tasty! Honestly, you really are a Filolial through and through!”
“Hmm… Filo, I’m going to throw this pebble lying here, and you fetch it. You did this with Shield Hero too, didn’t you?”
“Here? Okay!”

And so Crocodile Guy started throwing pebbles for Filo-tan to fetch. Argh… I wanted to go dive at Filo-tan so badly, but Rafumi was in the way, and right now I had Takt’s disposal to deal with. Rafumi turned her gaze toward Takt, sprawled on the ground.
“What is it? Are you here to interfere too?”
“Not at all. This man is an enemy of the world, scum who binds spirits against their will. He’s a target even that spirit would loathe. Well done, Spear Hero.”
“Wow… so you didn’t come out to defend him?”
“Why on earth would I defend this man? To begin with, he doesn’t treasure chocolate at all… no, he’s a target for total annihilation, having completely misunderstood the very concept of love.”
From what Rafumi said, it seemed Takt had a shockingly self-centered view of Valentine’s Day.
“Taking pride in how much chocolate you receive, that’s fine. But returning it with something so revolting is a complete desecration of chocolate itself.”
“Sounds like he’s breaking some rule of Rafumi-chan’s own personal code?”
“To begin with, this man feels nothing but carnal lust when he thinks of love. He’s an enemy to women. Well, the ones who flock around him are rotten to the soul as well.”
Rafumi turned her gaze toward Wolf’s Claw as well.

“It seems the Claw is satisfied, having left this detestable man’s hands and passed instead into the hands of someone tied to its previous wielder. See to it that you properly honor that spirit’s wishes.”
Apparently, there was no problem there.
“So, what punishment do you intend to hand down to this fool?”
“It’s already decided, I say. Rafumi, I won’t let you interfere.”
“I have no intention of interfering. I merely want him to taste the finest hell there is, for having desecrated a spirit.”
“Wow… so this is what they mean by ‘surrounded on all sides.’”
“I can’t exactly sympathize, but it is pitiful.”
“Indeed.”
“Kuun…”

And so, we hastily prepared the carriage and set off. Yuki-chan had kindly come along, so she pulled the carriage for us. We’d be traveling through the night. With the others taking turns running alongside Yuki-chan too, it made for quite a fun little stretch of time. Meanwhile, I figured I’d spend it thinking up ways to make Takt suffer. Oh, right—I also needed to include the torture of shaving off his fingers one by one while applying healing magic to treat the wounds along the way. With Paralyze Lance he wouldn’t be able to move, but I’d need to keep an eye on adjusting the paralytic poison so it didn’t cut off his sense of pain in the process.
